chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: Salva Sanders as a blues player and the western tours
summary: With the enlarged band Schoonover books a tour west; Salva Sanders keeps conservative habits and plays strong blues.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: So we went on and I began to get the right band sure enough, and as I said, Salva--I don't know, he was just terrific and he had a lot of experience, more than me, with these other bands, and he had been bandleader for one of those--not the Southern Serenaders, but I think for the Texas Rangers and he would play and at once we made a trip out west, Schoonover took us out on a tour out west, and of course by this time I had enlarged the band and everything and we really were cooking, making a little money, and Salva would have his games but he was very, very conservative, and they would have the poker games and all (inaudible). Rene was in the band then with Salva there and they were tight and they would work out things, you see Salva records all right (inaudible) and sometimes if we'd go round maybe a jam session and it looked like
somebody else was kind of cutting in, he would say, just let me play a blues and you talk about playing blues, he could play you the blues like--
(Side A of Tape 2 ended at this point. Transcript will continue in accordance with Side B.)
